Correlation: Langflow /api/v1/upload POST + cache file-creation spike (CVE-2026-55450) AIActions on Objectives High
Joins web access logs (POST to /api/v1/upload/) with filesystem events writing into the Langflow cache directory within the same 5-minute window — confirms the full attack chain (request → on-disk impact) and rules out unrelated cache growth from model loads, replicas, or backups. High-confidence variant for paging. Rationale: Per reviewer feedback #2 — UC1 and UC2 each have residual FP risk (legit bulk uploads can trip either alone), but the join collapses that to near zero: only a host that receives the unauthenticated POSTs AND writes the matching SHA256-named cache files in the same 5-minute bucket survives. Time-window correlation as per the KB pattern-time-window-correlation.
ATT&CKT1190 T1499.001
Data sourcesWeb Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authenticated post-upgrade (≥1.9.1) bulk-upload by a flow author with many large assets in one session
  • Migration tool ingesting flows and their cache artifacts together
  • Load test that exercises both /upload and the resulting file-write path
  • Backup restore that simultaneously serves API and replays cache files
  • Blue-team validation run that PoCs CVE-2026-55450 on a known host
Response runbook
1) Triage — verify the time-aligned Posts and Files are causally related (sample a few Web log src_ips and check whether the same flow_id UUID from the URI appears in the file path under <cache>/langflow/<flow_id>/). Confirm Langflow version is <1.9.1. 2) Contain — block source IPs from the Posts side at the WAF, gate the endpoint behind auth, free disk if under pressure, purge unauthorized flow_id directories. 3) Hunt — extend the join across the past 7d for any prior persistent abuser from the same /24; sweep TVM for vulnerable Langflow installs (<1.9.1) and prioritize internet-facing first; check whether response status was 201 (info leak occurred) on every survived row.
let UploadWin = 5m;
let Posts = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(24h)
  | where LocalPort == 7860
  | where RemoteIPType !in ("Loopback","Private")
  | summarize Conns = count(), SrcIPs = make_set(RemoteIP) by DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, UploadWin)
  | where Conns >= 5;
let Writes = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(24h)
  | where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed")
  | where FolderPath has_any ("/langflow/", @"\langflow\", "Caches/langflow", ".cache/langflow")
  | where FileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{32,}\."
  | summarize Files = count(), Bytes = sum(FileSize) by DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, UploadWin);
Posts
| join kind=inner Writes on DeviceName, Timestamp
| where Files >= 20
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, Conns, SrcIPs, Files, Bytes
| order by Timestamp desc
let UploadWin = 5m;
let Posts = CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
  | where RequestURL has "/api/v1/upload/"
  | summarize Posts = count(), SrcIPs = make_set(SourceIP), TotalIn = sum(toint(ReceivedBytes)) by HostName = tolower(DestinationHostName), bin(TimeGenerated, UploadWin)
  | where Posts >= 5;
let Writes = ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
  | where EventType == "FileCreated"
  | where TargetFilePath has "langflow"
  | where TargetFileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{32,}\."
  | summarize Files = count(), Bytes = sum(toint(TargetFileSize)) by HostName = tolower(DvcHostname), bin(TimeGenerated, UploadWin);
Posts
| join kind=inner Writes on HostName, TimeGenerated
| where Files >= 20
| project TimeGenerated, HostName, SrcIPs, Posts, TotalIn, Files, Bytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable Langflow exposed to network (CVE-2026-55450 inventory) AIReconnaissance High
Surfaces Langflow installations on tenant hosts with version <1.9.1 — the affected range per the GHSA — joined with DeviceInfo IsInternetFacing, so SOC can prioritise patching internet-reachable hosts before the exploitation UCs fire. Pre-exploit hygiene hunt. Rationale: Article gives the exact affected range (langflow <1.9.1) and CVE ID. TVM tables surface the vulnerable software inventory; joining DeviceInfo's IsInternetFacing gives SOC an immediate patch-priority list. Pre-exploit hunt, no attack telemetry required — the right place to start before the alerting UCs fire.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Langflow installed in a dev/test environment that's not actually exposed despite the IsInternetFacing flag (offline namespace)
  • Custom Langflow fork named 'langflow' but maintained internally with the patch backported
  • Stale TVM data — host was patched but inventory hasn't refreshed yet
  • Air-gapped lab host where the version string is intentionally left at <1.9.1
  • Pre-1.9.1 install on a host that's only reachable from a private VPC despite the IP being public-class
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareVersion !startswith "1.9.1" and SoftwareVersion !startswith "1.9.2" and SoftwareVersion !startswith "1.10"
Response runbook
1) Triage — confirm SoftwareVersion is genuinely <1.9.1 (string comparison can lie on pre-release tags like 1.9.0rc1); confirm IsInternetFacing by checking the public IP listens on TCP 7860 from outside. 2) Contain — coordinate with the platform owner to upgrade to 1.9.1 (fix is PR #12831); if upgrade can't happen same day, gate /api/v1/upload/* behind auth at the WAF or remove external exposure. 3) Hunt — pivot to UC1/UC2/UC3 historical search for any prior exploitation on the same hosts; check Langflow API access logs for prior anonymous POSTs to /api/v1/upload/ that would indicate the gap was already used.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-55450" or (SoftwareName =~ "langflow" and SoftwareVendor in~ ("langflow-ai", "langflow"))
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-55450" or SoftwareName =~ "langflow"
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| order by IsInternetFacing desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

DeviceProcessEvents

Crypto Clipper Campaign Abuses Fake Reviews, AI Narrators, and VirusTotal Comments

The Hacker News
2026-06-17 8 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

An unknown threat actor has been observed leveraging paid or promoted posts on legitimate news websites to drum up buzz for their warez, according to new findings from Check Point Research. The threat actor also has at their disposal a dedicated WordPress phishing page that acts as the central hub, alongside GitHub and SourceForge projects promoted by fake accounts, a YouTube channel, and a

ATT&CKT1021.001 T1190 T1486 T1555.003 T1566

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Crypto 'sniper bot' / Aviator Predictor lure download-and-execute from SourceForge or GitHub · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Crypto 'sniper bot' / Aviator Predictor lure download-and-execute from SourceForge or GitHub AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the Check Point Rust clipper campaign by correlating downloads of executables from SourceForge or GitHub whose filenames match the campaign's specific social-engineering lures (Solana/Pump.fun sniper bots, Aviator Predictor, crash-game predictors) with subsequent first execution from a user-writable path. The SHA256 join between the file-drop and process-execution events makes this article-specific rather than catching any crypto-themed tool a user happens to run. Rationale: The article explicitly names Solana sniper bots, Pump.fun sniper bots, Aviator Predictor, and crash-game predictors as the lure themes, with SourceForge and GitHub as the named distribution platforms — the FileOriginUrl + lure-token correlation ties endpoint detection back to the campaign's specific social-engineering hooks. Cross-checked The Hacker News and InfotechLead coverage and the clip.gif demo (showing the Notepad btc_wallet → wallet-app clipboard substitution) for behavioral confirmation; no public SHA256/wallet IOCs were available at search time, so this is a hunting-tier behavioral query. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/crypto-clipper-campaign-abuses-fake.html • https://infotechlead.com/security/cybercriminals-manipulate-github-youtube-and-virustotal-to-spread-crypto-stealing-malware-96613 • https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi-BtcZtH5fovAmDU_naao6gUXxP7z2gbzRS5dh0ihlwxmyvrKEOvVzkGwCndKLmeurQQ9gVebjrJynRkx8dJF858sS7Xqk9OL4diFcjia9zgBeRndSjrH6j_uuPTEzs2izOhZlS6FeCjtZV8IxCw96vTn1CUIx4nLOfpW7Y1FiRvtSdWovorzSgeK5FZfz/s1700-e365/clip.gif
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1608.001 T1583.006 T1657
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Crypto-savvy developer running a legitimate open-source Solana sniper bot from GitHub for personal trading
  • Malware analyst or threat researcher detonating a known crypto-clipper sample in a triage VM
  • Sports betting / fantasy analytics desktop tools whose filename literally contains 'predictor' (e.g. 'NFLPredictor.exe')
  • Game-development AI utilities packaged with names like 'CrashPredictor' for in-game economy testing
  • Red-team / purple-team engagement deliberately running the same campaign tooling for detection tuning
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msiexec.exe", "explorer.exe") and FolderPath has_any (@"\Program Files\", @"\Program Files (x86)\")) and not (ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ ("Microsoft Corporation", "Google LLC", "Mozilla Corporation", "Valve"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: Pull the SHA256 from the join and submit to VirusTotal + MalwareBazaar; verify FileOriginUrl resolves to a SourceForge project or GitHub repo with the boosted-but-shallow signals Check Point flagged (very recent commits, single-contributor, fake-looking stars). Ask the user via chat whether they intentionally downloaded a crypto trading or gambling tool. 2) Contain: Isolate the device in Defender/Falcon. Block the SHA256 organisation-wide via custom IOC. Force-reset any crypto wallet credentials the user used on that device and warn the user not to copy-paste wallet addresses until the host is rebuilt — the clipper substitutes addresses silently. 3) Hunt: Pivot org-wide on the SHA256 and the FileOriginUrl host; expand the lure-token regex to scan 60 days of DeviceFileEvents for sibling drops; check DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound HTTPS from the binary to the SourceForge/GitHub origin in case of an updater channel.
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let LureTokens = dynamic(["sniper","pumpfun","pump.fun","aviator","predictor","solana-bot","solanabot","crash-predictor","crashpredictor"]);
let SuspectOriginHosts = dynamic(["sourceforge.net","sf.net","github.com","github.io","githubusercontent.com","raw.githubusercontent.com"]);
let SuspectDrops = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
    | where FileName endswith ".exe" or FileName endswith ".msi" or FileName endswith ".zip" or FileName endswith ".dmg" or FileName endswith ".pkg" or FileName endswith ".app"
    | where isnotempty(FileOriginUrl)
    | where tolower(FileOriginUrl) has_any (SuspectOriginHosts)
    | extend NameLower = tolower(FileName)
    | where NameLower has_any (LureTokens)
    | project DropTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, DroppedFolder = FolderPath, DroppedName = FileName, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\Downloads\", @"\AppData\", @"\Public\", "/Users/", "/Applications/", "/tmp/")
| join kind=inner SuspectDrops on $left.DeviceId == $right.DeviceId, $left.SHA256 == $right.SHA256
| where Timestamp >= DropTime
| extend DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, DropTime)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, DropTime, DelayMinutes, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let LureRegex = @"(?i)(sniper|pump[\.\-_]?fun|aviator|predictor|solana[\-_]?bot|crash[\-_]?predictor)";
let UserPathRegex = @"(?i)\\(Users|Downloads|AppData|Public|Temp)\\";
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetProcessName matches regex LureRegex
| where TargetProcessName matches regex UserPathRegex
| where TargetProcessName endswith ".exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Crypto Sniper Bot or Aviator Predictor Lure Execution from User-Writable Path
id: 5b8c2f3a-9d41-4e6c-a2b7-1f9c8e3d5072
description: Detects execution of binaries whose names match the Check Point crypto clipper campaign's social-engineering lures (Solana/Pump.fun sniper bots, Aviator Predictor, crash-game predictors) from user-writable paths typically used for downloads.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/crypto-clipper-campaign-abuses-fake.html
  - https://infotechlead.com/security/cybercriminals-manipulate-github-youtube-and-virustotal-to-spread-crypto-stealing-malware-96613
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1657
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_name:
    Image|contains:
      - 'sniper'
      - 'pumpfun'
      - 'pump.fun'
      - 'aviator'
      - 'predictor'
      - 'solana-bot'
      - 'solanabot'
      - 'crash-predictor'
      - 'crashpredictor'
  selection_path:
    Image|contains:
      - '\Users\'
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\AppData\'
      - '\Public\'
      - '\Temp\'
  condition: selection_name and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate open-source Solana trading bots run by crypto-savvy users
  - Security researchers detonating samples in a sandbox VM
  - Sports analytics or game-AI tools whose filename contains 'predictor'
level: medium
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) (@Image:(*sniper* OR *Sniper* OR *SNIPER* OR *pumpfun* OR *PumpFun* OR *pump.fun* OR *Pump.Fun* OR *aviator* OR *Aviator* OR *predictor* OR *Predictor* OR *solana-bot* OR *Solana-Bot* OR *solanabot* OR *crash-predictor* OR *Crash-Predictor*)) AND @Image:(*\\Users\\* OR *\\Downloads\\* OR *\\AppData\\* OR *\\Public\\*) AND -@User:*$
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(sniper|pump[._-]?fun|aviator|predictor|solana[._-]?bot|crash[._-]?predictor)/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(Users|Downloads|AppData|Public|Temp)\\/i
| ImageFileName=/\.exe$/i
| UserName!=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, SHA256HashData], function=[count(), min(@timestamp, as=FirstSeen), max(@timestamp, as=LastSeen), collect([CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName])])

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as drop_path values(Filesystem.file_hash) as drop_sha256 from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created (Filesystem.file_name="*sniper*" OR Filesystem.file_name="*pumpfun*" OR Filesystem.file_name="*pump.fun*" OR Filesystem.file_name="*aviator*" OR Filesystem.file_name="*predictor*" OR Filesystem.file_name="*solana*bot*" OR Filesystem.file_name="*crash*predictor*") (Filesystem.file_name="*.exe" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.msi" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.zip" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.dmg" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.pkg") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename file_hash as sha256 | join sha256 [| tstats summariesonly=false count as exec_count values(Processes.process) as exec_cmdline values(Processes.process_path) as exec_path values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_path="*\\Users\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Public\\*") Processes.user!="*$" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process_hash as sha256] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | table firstTime lastTime dest user file_name drop_path sha256 exec_path exec_cmdline parent exec_count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'

level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

            - '\wscript.exe'

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High

ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName

// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Critical

Junior Hacker Used Tailscale and OpenSSH to Keep Access After His C2 Went Offline

The Hacker News
2026-06-17 18 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A French-speaking attacker broke into a small French automotive business, planted a keylogger, and stole banking and email credentials. Ordinary stuff, until one move near the end. Before his command-and-control server went dark, he installed OpenSSH and Tailscale on a victim's machine, building a way back in that did not run through the C2 at all. When the Havoc server went offline the next

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] certutil smart-card / certificate store enumeration
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] wscript/cscript executing .vbs from user staging folder (Poisson VBScript stager)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Junior Hacker Used Tailscale and OpenSSH to Keep Access After His C2 Went Offlin
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] OpenSSH Server install on Windows workstation (Poisson persistence pivot) · [LLM] Logon-trigger scheduled task at HIGHEST privileges launching script interpreter · [LLM] authorized_keys file write on Windows host (SSH key persistence) · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Tailscale client install or tailnet connection (100.100.100.0/8 / login.tailscale.com) · [LLM] SSH reverse tunnel (ssh -R) outbound from Windows endpoint · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] powercfg disabling standby/hibernate to keep host harvest-ready · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change
OpenSSH Server install on Windows workstation (Poisson persistence pivot) AIInstallation High
Detects Add-WindowsCapability adding the OpenSSH.Server feature, sshd.exe service start, or registry/firewall configuration enabling sshd on a Windows endpoint. Article-specific: Poisson installed OpenSSH on April 7 as a C2-independent reentry path so access survived the Havoc takedown. Rationale: Cato's first hunt-list item is literally 'OpenSSH Server installs on a Windows workstation, which is rarely legitimate.' Defender ships OpenSSH as a FoD capability — Add-WindowsCapability/dism/sshd.exe are the three install vectors; combining them with non-machine accounts keeps this near-zero FP.
ATT&CKT1133 T1021.004 T1505
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dev/SRE workstation where the user genuinely needs sshd to test Ansible/Terraform from WSL
  • IT pilot enabling RemoteSSH for management at scale
  • Visual Studio Code 'Remote-SSH' setup wizard installing the OpenSSH client (not server)
  • Lab/test image being provisioned by Packer
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("MsiExec.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe") and AccountName !in~ ("SYSTEM","LOCAL SERVICE","NETWORK SERVICE")
Response runbook
Triage: pivot on the host's last 24h DeviceProcessEvents — look for VBS->PowerShell->.NET chain (Havoc Demon staging), Tailscale process, RustDesk install, schtasks /Create at logon, and any keylogger artifact under user staging dirs. Check DeviceLogonEvents for new inbound RemoteInteractive logons after install. Contain: stop the sshd service, disable the OpenSSH.Server capability, remove host firewall allow rule for TCP/22, block egress to login.tailscale.com and DuckDNS at edge, isolate the host. Hunt: across the org, query for tailscale.exe execution, ssh.exe with -R flag, schtasks /RL HIGHEST /SC ONLOGON launching script interpreters, and powercfg standby-timeout-* 0 over the same 30d window.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Add-WindowsCapability","OpenSSH.Server","Start-Service sshd","Set-Service -Name sshd"))
   or (FileName =~ "dism.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "OpenSSH")
   or FileName =~ "sshd.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountType =~ "User"
| where (NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("Add-WindowsCapability","OpenSSH.Server","Start-Service sshd"))
   or (NewProcessName endswith @"\dism.exe" and CommandLine has "OpenSSH")
   or NewProcessName endswith @"\sshd.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: OpenSSH Server Capability Install on Windows Workstation

source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) ((@Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\dism.exe OR *\DISM.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*Add-WindowsCapability* OR *OpenSSH.Server* OR *"Start-Service sshd"*)) OR @Image:(*\sshd.exe OR *\SSHD.EXE))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ImageFileName=/\\sshd\.exe$/i OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|dism)\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(Add-WindowsCapability|OpenSSH\.Server|Start-Service\s+sshd)/i)) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=powershell.exe OR Processes.process_name=pwsh.exe) AND (Processes.process="*Add-WindowsCapability*OpenSSH.Server*" OR Processes.process="*Set-Service*sshd*Automatic*" OR Processes.process="*Start-Service*sshd*") OR Processes.process_name=sshd.exe OR (Processes.process_name=dism.exe AND Processes.process="*OpenSSH*") by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | sort - firstTime

Tailscale client install or tailnet connection (100.100.100.0/8 / login.tailscale.com) AICommand & Control High
Surfaces tailscale.exe/tailscaled.exe execution, tailscale-up commands, DNS for login.tailscale.com, or any traffic into the 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT / 100.100.100.0/24 magic-DNS range. Article-specific: Poisson joined victim machines to his private tailnet for a fully out-of-band reentry path that survived the Havoc takedown. Rationale: Cato names Tailscale outright as Poisson's 'separate door' and the article gives the magic-DNS IP 100.100.100.2 and login.tailscale.com as pivot indicators. The detection joins process telemetry (tailscale.exe/up/login) and network telemetry (100.100.100/24, port 41641, control-plane DNS) so it catches the install AND the active tunnel.
ATT&CKT1572 T1219 T1090
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Engineering team using Tailscale as their official corporate VPN
  • Remote SRE accessing infra over a documented tailnet
  • Personal Tailscale install on a BYOD/AAD-registered laptop that's also on the corp tenant
  • Tailscale being silently bundled by another tool like Headscale or NextDNS
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in (dynamic(["<approved-tailscale-hosts>"])) and InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("SYSTEM","<corp-IT-deployment-account>")
Response runbook
Triage: confirm whether the host is in IT's Tailscale-approved inventory; if not, pull DeviceProcessEvents 24h before/after the install for a Havoc/RustDesk staging chain and check DeviceLogonEvents for inbound RemoteInteractive over 100.x.x.x. Contain: kill tailscaled, uninstall the package, block login.tailscale.com + controlplane.tailscale.com + derp*.tailscale.com at proxy, deny 100.64.0.0/10 egress at edge, revoke the tailnet auth key if obtainable. Hunt: pivot org-wide for any host that resolved login.tailscale.com over the past 90d but is not on the approved list; correlate with OpenSSH installs and powercfg standby changes on the same host.
let TS_Proc = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("tailscale.exe","tailscaled.exe")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has_any (" up --authkey"," up --login-server","tailscale login","tailscale up") and ProcessCommandLine has "tailscale")
   or FolderPath has @"\Tailscale\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName;
let TS_Net = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("login.tailscale.com","controlplane.tailscale.com","derp.tailscale.com")
   or RemoteIP startswith "100.100.100."
   or (RemotePort == 41641 and RemoteIPType == "Public")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
union isfuzzy=true TS_Proc, TS_Net
| order by Timestamp desc
let TS_Proc = SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\tailscale.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\tailscaled.exe" or CommandLine has_any ("tailscale up","tailscale login","--authkey")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName;
let TS_Net = DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Name has_any ("login.tailscale.com","controlplane.tailscale.com","derp")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name;
union isfuzzy=true TS_Proc, TS_Net
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: b8e3facd-4f9c-4f2b-ac7f-3d6e9f8a2b5c
description: Detects tailscale.exe/tailscaled.exe execution or tailnet bootstrap commands on a Windows endpoint, per Cato CTRL's hunt for 'Poisson's' Tailscale fallback channel.
references:

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ImageFileName=/\\tailscale(d)?\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/(tailscale\s+(up|login)|--authkey|--login-server)/i) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=tailscale.exe OR Processes.process_name=tailscaled.exe OR Processes.process="*tailscale*up*" OR Processes.process="*tailscale*login*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_ip=100.64.0.0/10 OR All_Traffic.dest="login.tailscale.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="controlplane.tailscale.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_port=41641 by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`] | sort - count

SSH reverse tunnel (ssh -R) outbound from Windows endpoint AICommand & Control High
Detects ssh.exe invoked with `-R <port>` (remote-port-forward) to an external host — the technique Poisson used to expose victim ports back through his SSH listener. Tier alerting because ssh.exe with -R on a workstation is overwhelmingly attacker tradecraft. Rationale: Cato's hunt list calls out 'ssh -R reverse tunnels heading to outside hosts' verbatim. The regex `-R <bind>:<port>` keys on Poisson's actual SSH-listener setup; pairing with `AccountName !endswith "$"` and `ssh.exe` on a workstation (vs. server) keeps the FP cone tight.
ATT&CKT1572 T1021.004 T1571
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer using ngrok-style SSH reverse tunnel to expose a local dev server
  • DevOps engineer port-forwarding through a bastion for debugging
  • GitHub Actions self-hosted runner setup script
  • Educational SSH tutorial run by a curious user
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("code.exe","WindowsTerminal.exe","git-bash.exe") and DeviceName !startswith "DEV-"
Response runbook
Triage: extract the destination from `ReverseSpec` — passive-DNS / WHOIS / abuse.ch checks on the bind host; pull DeviceNetworkEvents from that host for the same time window. Contain: kill the ssh.exe process tree, block the destination IP at egress, rotate any private keys cached in %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\ on the host. Hunt: cross-org search for ssh.exe -R, OpenSSH server installs, and Tailscale activations on the same host within 30 days — Poisson chained all three.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "ssh.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(^|\s)-R\s+(\S*:)?\d{1,5}(:[^\s]+:\d{1,5})?"
| extend ReverseSpec = extract(@"(?i)(?:^|\s)-R\s+(\S+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, ReverseSpec, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountType =~ "User"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\ssh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(^|\s)-R\s+(\S*:)?\d{1,5}"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SSH Reverse Tunnel Outbound from Windows Endpoint

wscript/cscript executing .vbs from user staging folder (Poisson VBScript stager) AIDelivery High
Detects wscript.exe or cscript.exe running a .vbs script out of Downloads, Temp, AppData, Public, or ProgramData — the exact pattern Cato calls out for Poisson's sandbox-evasion stager that decrypted the PowerShell loader. Tier alerting given the script-from-staging-folder combo is rarely legitimate. Rationale: Cato's hunt list: 'wscript.exe running .vbs files out of user staging folders.' The article also notes the stager had a 'sandbox-evasion delay' before decrypting the PowerShell loader — narrowing path-prefix to Downloads/Temp/AppData covers Poisson's drop spots without firing on legitimate GPO logon scripts in System32 or NETLOGON.
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1204.002 T1497.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vendor installer that drops a one-off .vbs cleanup script to %TEMP%
  • Adobe/Citrix uninstaller using a VBScript in ProgramData
  • Legacy ERP/accounting client launching a per-user .vbs from AppData
  • User opening an email-attached invoice (still suspicious — likely a true positive in disguise)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","installer.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: capture the .vbs file and the parent process — was it Outlook, browser, archive utility (WinRAR/7z), or a service? Decode the VBScript looking for the AES/XOR-decrypted PowerShell second stage Cato describes. Contain: kill wscript.exe tree, quarantine the .vbs file and its source archive, isolate the host. Hunt: pivot on the file SHA256, parent-process tree (was it spawned by a browser/mail client?), and any subsequent PowerShell → .NET in-memory loader spawns on the same host within 1h.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".vbs"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Pictures\", @"\Music\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountType =~ "User"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\wscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\cscript.exe"
| where CommandLine has ".vbs"
| where CommandLine has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\ProgramData\")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

powercfg disabling standby/hibernate to keep host harvest-ready AIActions on Objectives High
Detects powercfg.exe being used to set standby-timeout, hibernate-timeout, monitor-timeout or disk-timeout to 0 — Poisson's trick to prevent the machine sleeping so the local-file keylogger never pauses and he could hand-fetch the keystroke logs. Rationale: Cato's hunt list ends with 'powercfg standby-timeout changes that keep machines awake' — this is the literal article string. Combining standby-timeout/hibernate-timeout/-h off with a zero/off value is the operator-specific shape; powercfg called any other way (e.g. /list, /query) doesn't trip.
ATT&CKT1056.001 T1112 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT helpdesk script that disables sleep on conference-room/kiosk machines
  • Visual Studio installer toggling sleep during long compiles
  • Backup software (Veeam, Acronis) pinning the host awake during a job window
  • Power management GPO push from SCCM
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe","veeam.backup.shell.exe","sccm.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: who is the AccountName — a sysadmin or a regular user? Pull DeviceFileEvents for new files matching keylogger patterns (*.log/*.txt being appended-to-only by a Python or rundll32 process) and DeviceProcessEvents for python.exe / pythonw.exe spawning from non-standard paths. Contain: revert powercfg ('powercfg -change standby-timeout-ac 20'), isolate the host pending IR. Hunt: across the org for the same powercfg → keylogger file-write pair within 24h and for python.exe processes with PIDs that persist across logon/logoff.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "powercfg.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("standby-timeout","hibernate-timeout","monitor-timeout","disk-timeout","-change","/change","-setacvalueindex","-setdcvalueindex","-h off","/h off")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\s|-)0(\b|$)" or ProcessCommandLine has " off"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountType =~ "User"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\powercfg.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("standby-timeout","hibernate-timeout","monitor-timeout","disk-timeout","-change","/change","-h off")
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s0(\b|$)" or CommandLine has " off"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=powercfg.exe AND (Processes.process="*standby-timeout*" OR Processes.process="*hibernate-timeout*" OR Processes.process="*monitor-timeout*" OR Processes.process="*disk-timeout*" OR Processes.process="*-change*" OR Processes.process="*-setacvalueindex*" OR Processes.process="*-setdcvalueindex*" OR Processes.process="*-h off*") AND Processes.process="* 0*" by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | sort - firstTime

Logon-trigger scheduled task at HIGHEST privileges launching script interpreter AIInstallation High
Detects schtasks /Create or PowerShell Register-ScheduledTask creating a task with /SC ONLOGON and /RL HIGHEST that runs a script interpreter (powershell/pwsh/wscript/cscript/mshta/rundll32/regsvr32) — Poisson's pinning technique for at-every-logon highest-privilege persistence. Rationale: Cato's hunt list directly: 'scheduled tasks set to the highest privileges that launch script interpreters.' Three required tokens (Create + HIGHEST + ONLOGON) plus an interpreter payload are vanishingly rare in legitimate management tooling — GPO-deployed tasks typically use SYSTEM, not /RL HIGHEST from a user context.
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1547 T1078.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • RMM agent (NinjaOne/Datto) registering a logon healthcheck task
  • Citrix/VMware EUC client provisioning script
  • Custom IT logon banner script deployed by a sysadmin
  • Java auto-update logon trigger
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe","agent.exe","ninjarmm.exe","datto.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: dump the created task XML (`schtasks /Query /TN <name> /XML`), capture the script payload, decode any base64 / -EncodedCommand inside. Contain: delete the task (`schtasks /Delete /TN <name> /F`), revoke and re-test the user account, quarantine any payload files referenced. Hunt: pull all Security 4698 events on the host for the last 60d, cross-reference with DeviceFileEvents for the task's Action path, and search the org for tasks with the same name, author, or payload SHA256.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/Create","/CREATE","-Create")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/RL HIGHEST","/RL Highest","-RunLevel Highest")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/SC ONLOGON","/SC OnLogon","ONLOGON","-Trigger")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("powershell","pwsh","wscript","cscript","mshta","rundll32","regsvr32",".vbs",".js",".ps1","cmd.exe /c","cmd /c")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountType =~ "User"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("/Create","-Create")
| where CommandLine has "HIGHEST"
| where CommandLine has "ONLOGON"
| where CommandLine has_any ("powershell","pwsh","wscript","cscript","mshta","rundll32","regsvr32",".vbs",".ps1")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Logon-Trigger Scheduled Task at HIGHEST Privileges Launching Script Interpreter
id: fcf7be01-8fdf-4f6f-efbd-7fb0dcfce6f9
description: schtasks.exe creating an ONLOGON task with /RL HIGHEST whose action invokes a script interpreter — Poisson's at-every-logon persistence pattern from the Cato CTRL writeup.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/junior-hacker-used-tailscale-and.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1053.005
  - attack.t1547
  - attack.t1078.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'Create'
      - 'HIGHEST'
      - 'ONLOGON'
  payloads:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'powershell'
      - 'pwsh'
      - 'wscript'
      - 'cscript'
      - 'mshta'
      - 'rundll32'
      - 'regsvr32'
      - '.vbs'
      - '.ps1'
      - '.js'
  condition: selection and payloads
level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) @Image:(*\schtasks.exe OR *\SCHTASKS.EXE OR *\Schtasks.exe) @CommandLine:(*Create* AND *HIGHEST* AND *ONLOGON* AND (*powershell* OR *PowerShell* OR *pwsh* OR *wscript* OR *cscript* OR *mshta* OR *rundll32* OR *regsvr32* OR *.vbs* OR *.ps1*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i CommandLine=/Create/i CommandLine=/HIGHEST/i CommandLine=/ONLOGON/i CommandLine=/(powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|\.vbs|\.ps1|\.js)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=schtasks.exe AND Processes.process="*/Create*" AND Processes.process="*/RL*HIGHEST*" AND Processes.process="*/SC*ONLOGON*" AND (Processes.process="*powershell*" OR Processes.process="*pwsh*" OR Processes.process="*wscript*" OR Processes.process="*cscript*" OR Processes.process="*mshta*" OR Processes.process="*rundll32*" OR Processes.process="*regsvr32*" OR Processes.process="*.vbs*" OR Processes.process="*.ps1*" OR Processes.process="*.js*") by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=schtasks.exe AND Processes.process="*/Create*" AND Processes.process="*/RL*HIGHEST*" AND Processes.process="*/SC*ONLOGON*" AND (Processes.process="*powershell*" OR Processes.process="*pwsh*" OR Processes.process="*wscript*" OR Processes.process="*cscript*" OR Processes.process="*mshta*" OR Processes.process="*rundll32*" OR Processes.process="*regsvr32*" OR Processes.process="*.vbs*" OR Processes.process="*.ps1*" OR Processes.process="*.js*") by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | sort - firstTime
authorized_keys file write on Windows host (SSH key persistence) AIInstallation High
Detects creation or modification of `authorized_keys` under any user `.ssh\` directory or under `%ProgramData%\ssh\` — the file Poisson populated to make his key-based SSH reentry persistent. Tier alerting because authorized_keys writes on a Windows endpoint are nearly always operator-grade. Rationale: The article describes Poisson setting up 'key-based SSH' as the reentry path that survived the C2 takedown — the persistence anchor is the authorized_keys file. On Windows the canonical paths are `%USERPROFILE%\.ssh\authorized_keys` and `%ProgramData%\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys`; either being written by anything other than the user's interactive ssh-keygen flow is suspicious.
ATT&CKT1098.004 T1021.004 T1078.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer setting up SSH access to a GitHub repo and writing their own pubkey
  • IT staff bootstrapping an Ansible/SaltStack control node
  • Visual Studio Code Remote-SSH key copy during initial setup
  • User running ssh-copy-id from WSL
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ssh-keygen.exe","notepad.exe","code.exe","explorer.exe") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","pwsh.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: read the authorized_keys file contents — capture every pubkey present and the comments/notes. Pull DeviceLogonEvents for successful SSH inbound logons referencing those keys in the last 30d. Contain: delete the offending lines (or the file), restart sshd, rotate the local user password, force expire any current SSH sessions. Hunt: across the org for authorized_keys writes whose ActingProcess is not ssh-keygen/notepad/code; correlate with Tailscale and OpenSSH-install events on the same host within 7d.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName =~ "authorized_keys"
   or FolderPath endswith @"\.ssh\authorized_keys"
   or FolderPath has @"\ProgramData\ssh\"
   or FolderPath has @"\Windows\System32\config\systemprofile\.ssh\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountDomain
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName =~ "authorized_keys"
   or TargetFilePath endswith @"\.ssh\authorized_keys"
   or TargetFilePath has @"\ProgramData\ssh\"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SSH authorized_keys File Written on Windows Host
id: 0df8cf12-9faf-4f80-faec-8fc1edfdf70a
description: Creation/modification of an OpenSSH authorized_keys file on a Windows endpoint — the persistence step Poisson used to lock in key-based SSH reentry.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/junior-hacker-used-tailscale-and.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1098.004
  - attack.t1021.004
  - attack.t1078.003
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\authorized_keys'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.ssh\'
      - '\ProgramData\ssh\'
  condition: selection_name or selection_path
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(11 OR 4663) @TargetFilename:(*\\authorized_keys OR *\\.ssh\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\ssh\\* OR *\\.SSH\\*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten (TargetFileName=/\\authorized_keys$/i OR TargetFileName=/\\\.ssh\\/i OR TargetFileName=/\\ProgramData\\ssh\\/i) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="authorized_keys" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\authorized_keys*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\ProgramData\\ssh\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Windows\\System32\\config\\systemprofile\\.ssh\\*") AND Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","renamed") by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="authorized_keys" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\authorized_keys*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\ProgramData\\ssh\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Windows\\System32\\config\\systemprofile\\.ssh\\*") AND Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","renamed") by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort - firstTime
certutil smart-card / certificate store enumeration AIReconnaissance Medium
Detects certutil.exe (or PowerShell Cert: drive enumeration) being used to enumerate Personal/Smart-card cert stores or query CSP/smartcard info — Poisson's late-stage move that Cato reads as recon for certificate-based logins. Rationale: Article: 'probed smart-card and certificate stores (a sign he was eyeing certificate-based logins).' certutil -store/-scinfo/-csplist are the canonical Windows ways to enumerate user/machine cert stores and smart-card CSPs; explicitly excluding the common LOLBin uses (-urlcache, -decode, -hashfile) keeps signal high.
ATT&CKT1555.004 T1552.004 T1087.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT/PKI admin auditing local cert stores before a smart-card rollout
  • Developer querying Cert:\CurrentUser\My from PowerShell for code-signing
  • Group Policy applying machine-cert auto-enrollment
  • Vendor MSI installer validating its signing cert pre-install
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe","sccm.exe","intunemgmt.exe") and AccountName !in~ ("<pki-admin-account>")
Response runbook
Triage: confirm who/what spawned certutil — interactive cmd/PowerShell vs. a service. Pull the same host's DeviceProcessEvents for nearby Havoc/Demon staging behavior (PowerShell with -nop, .NET in-memory loader, shellcode injection into explorer.exe). Contain: if interactive and non-IT, isolate and force interactive logon revalidation; if the user has smart-card auth issued, rotate it. Hunt: across the org, look for the same user account hitting Cert:/certutil -store on multiple hosts within 24h and for any subsequent klist/kerberos ticket use that doesn't match a normal logon flow.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (FileName =~ "certutil.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-store","-scinfo","-SCInfo","-csplist","-csptest","-key","-user My","-user Root"))
   or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My","Cert:\\LocalMachine\\My","Get-ChildItem Cert:","ls Cert:","dir Cert:"))
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "-urlcache" and ProcessCommandLine !has "-decode" and ProcessCommandLine !has "-encode" and ProcessCommandLine !has "-hashfile"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountType =~ "User"
| where (NewProcessName endswith @"\certutil.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("-store","-scinfo","-csplist","-csptest","-key","-user My"))
   or ((NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has "Cert:\\")
| where CommandLine !has "-urlcache" and CommandLine !has "-decode" and CommandLine !has "-hashfile"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: certutil or PowerShell Certificate Store Enumeration
id: 1ef9da23-afa0-4f91-fbfd-9fd2fdfaf81b
description: certutil -store/-scinfo/-csplist or PowerShell Cert:\\ drive enumeration — recon for certificate-based / smart-card logins, the final-week move in the Cato CTRL writeup on 'Poisson'.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/junior-hacker-used-tailscale-and.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1555.004
  - attack.t1552.004
  - attack.t1087.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_certutil:
    Image|endswith: '\certutil.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-store'
      - '-scinfo'
      - '-csplist'
      - '-csptest'
      - '-key'
  selection_ps:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Cert:\CurrentUser\My'
      - 'Cert:\LocalMachine\My'
      - 'Get-ChildItem Cert:'
  filter:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-urlcache'
      - '-decode'
      - '-encode'
      - '-hashfile'
      - '-verify'
  condition: (1 of selection_*) and not filter
level: medium
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) ((@Image:(*\certutil.exe OR *\CertUtil.exe OR *\CERTUTIL.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*-store* OR *-scinfo* OR *-SCInfo* OR *-csplist* OR *-csptest*) AND NOT @CommandLine:(*-urlcache* OR *-decode* OR *-encode* OR *-hashfile*)) OR (@Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe) AND @CommandLine:(*"Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My"* OR *"Cert:\\LocalMachine\\My"*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ((ImageFileName=/\\certutil\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(-store|-scinfo|-csplist|-csptest|-key|-user\s+My)/i AND NOT CommandLine=/(-urlcache|-decode|-encode|-hashfile|-verify)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/Cert:\\\\(CurrentUser|LocalMachine)\\\\My/i)) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=certutil.exe AND (Processes.process="*-store*" OR Processes.process="*-scinfo*" OR Processes.process="*-csplist*" OR Processes.process="*-csptest*" OR Processes.process="*-key*" OR Processes.process="*-user*My*")) OR ((Processes.process_name=powershell.exe OR Processes.process_name=pwsh.exe) AND (Processes.process="*Get-ChildItem*Cert:*" OR Processes.process="*ls*Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My*" OR Processes.process="*Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My*")) by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | where NOT match(process, "(?i)-urlcache|-decode|-encode|-hashfile|-verify") | sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=certutil.exe AND (Processes.process="*-store*" OR Processes.process="*-scinfo*" OR Processes.process="*-csplist*" OR Processes.process="*-csptest*" OR Processes.process="*-key*" OR Processes.process="*-user*My*")) OR ((Processes.process_name=powershell.exe OR Processes.process_name=pwsh.exe) AND (Processes.process="*Get-ChildItem*Cert:*" OR Processes.process="*ls*Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My*" OR Processes.process="*Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My*")) by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | where NOT match(process, "(?i)-urlcache|-decode|-encode|-hashfile|-verify") | sort - firstTime
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("100.100.100.2") or RemoteUrl has_any ("duckdns.org", "login.tailscale.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,

let BadIPs     = dynamic(["100.100.100.2"]);

ImNetworkSession

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")

ImFileEvent

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"

      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m

| where files > 200
| sort - files

      AND (Filesystem.file_name IN ("tailscale.exe"))
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]
Critical

Malicious JetBrains Plugins Steal AI API Keys as Chrome Extensions Capture Chatbot Chats

The Hacker News
2026-06-17 9 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have flagged a "coordinated malware campaign" on the JetBrains Marketplace that has published no less than 15 malicious plugins capable of exfiltrating artificial intelligence (AI) provider keys. "Every plugin poses as an AI coding assistant built on DeepSeek and other large language models, offering chat, commit messages, code review, bug finding, and unit tests,"
